section.sectionSummaryBrief: To reach the level above even the aspect of "I, Hashem, have not changed," one must specifically serve with one's own power, for through such service a true delight is generated Above, drawing from the innermost dimension.
section.t: And in order to reach this level, which is above even the aspect of "I, Hashem, have not changed,"
this is specifically through service with one's own power.
For behold,
even though "if you are righteous, what do you give Him," etc.,
nevertheless,
service is a need of the Most High,
and as our sages, of blessed memory, said,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moshe, "You should have helped Me,"
immediately [Moshe] said to Him, "And now, please let the power of my Lord be great,"
and as is explained in the discourses
on the verse "And now, please let the power of my Lord be great,"
that there is an aspect of "the power of my Lord" in its own right,
and through service, the magnification in "the power of my Lord" is effected.
And the explanation is,
as it is written,
"You yearn for the work of Your hands,"
"yearn" is an expression of delight,
and since constant delight is not delight,
therefore,
only through service below with one's own power,
which is a matter of renewal,
is true delight Above effected,
and therefore specifically through this is the drawing down from the aspect of the innermost dimension effected.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: When the Holy One chose Yaakov and his sons, He established for them a Rosh Chodesh of redemption, because through service with one's own power one reaches the innermost dimension above even the natural order, from which miraculous governance is drawn.
section.t: And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said: When the Holy One, blessed be He, chose His world, He established in it new moons and years, and when He chose Yaakov and his sons, He established for them a Rosh Chodesh of redemption.
For,
the initial coming into being of the worlds was from His own essence,
because "He desires kindness,"
and not from the side of man's service,
and as it is written,
"and there was no man to work the ground"
(and only afterwards was the order established of "a mist arose from the earth and watered the entire face of the ground").
Therefore,
even though the coming into being from the aspect of "He desires kindness" is from the aspect of kindness that is above the chain of descent,
and even up to the aspect of "He desires kindness" as it is before the contraction,
this is only from the aspect of externality,
and from there is drawn natural governance in a manner of "they shall not cease,"
in which is revealed the matter of "I, Hashem, have not changed,"
the aspect of externality.
And when He chose Yaakov and his sons,
when the matter of service with one's own power began,
through which one effects true delight Above
("You yearn for the work of Your hands"),
then one reaches the aspect of the innermost dimension, which is above even the aspect of "I, Hashem, have not changed,"
and from there is drawn miraculous governance,
a Rosh Chodesh of redemption.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The connection between miraculous governance and Rosh Chodesh is explained through the difference between the sun's constant cycle and the moon's renewal, corresponding to external versus internal union, with Rosh Chodesh representing the internal union that draws a new light from above the chain of descent.
section.t: And based on this, one can explain the connection of miraculous governance to the general concept of Rosh Chodesh,
for Rosh Chodesh Nissan
(the new year for miraculous governance)
is the head of the months.
And with an introduction of the explanation of the statement of the Ibn Ezra, "The moon has no year at all, just as the sun has no month at all,"
for seemingly,
since the course of both of them
(the moon and the sun)
is in a manner that they constantly return and revolve, etc.,
what is the difference between them that a year is specifically related to the sun and a month is specifically related to the moon,
for the moon also revolves and proceeds constantly as before?
And the explanation is simply,
that in the course of the sun there is no change or renewal
(for each year it returns and revolves as before,
"year" [shanah] from the term "repetition" [mishnah]),
but not so the course of the moon, which is in a manner that has change and renewal,
for during the days of the month the moon changes from smallness to greatness,
for at the beginning of the month it is in smallness,
and from day to day it grows until the middle of the month,
and afterwards it diminishes until at the end of the month it is completely hidden,
and afterwards the new moon is born anew,
therefore it is called "month" [chodesh],
from the term "renewal" [chiddush],
for it receives new light from the sun.
And this is the matter of the union of the sun and the moon that occurs on Rosh Chodesh,
which is an internal union,
for although the union of the sun and the moon is a constant matter that exists throughout the month,
for the moon always receives its light from the sun,
nevertheless,
this is only an external union,
and its beginning and origin is on Rosh Chodesh,
for then it is a union of the sun and the moon, an internal union
[And regarding internal union,
behold, about this our sages, of blessed memory, said,
"The Holy One, blessed be He, does not enter the lower Jerusalem until He enters the upper Jerusalem."]
And this is also the difference between natural governance and miraculous governance,
that constant governance is drawn through an external union,
which is a constant union,
and miraculous governance is drawn through an internal union,
a revelation of new light that is drawn from an aspect that is entirely above the chain of descent.
And concerning this it is said, "This month is for you the head of the months," etc.,
that Rosh Chodesh, whose concept is internal union,
is related to miraculous governance,
a Rosh Chodesh of redemption.
